subject: Materials Science
title: Interstitials: Atoms in the Wrong Place
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Interstitials: Atoms in the Wrong Place.

hook.text: Squeeze a small atom into the gap between bigger ones and the crystal bulges and strains.

buildup.text: An interstitial defect is an extra atom wedged into a space between regular lattice sites.

discovery.text: Carbon atoms in iron sit in interstitial sites — they're small enough to fit in BCC octahedral holes.

twist.text: Interstitials strain the lattice and block dislocation motion — that's why carbon makes iron into steel.

climax.text: Just 0.8% carbon transforms soft iron into high-carbon steel strong enough for swords and springs.

punchline.text: A tiny atom in the wrong spot can transform an entire material.

quiz.question: How does carbon strengthen iron?
options: It replaces iron atoms in the lattice
It sits in interstitial sites and blocks dislocation movement
It melts and fills cracks in the iron
